name: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc.
owner_fcf_base: Owner FCF = FY2025 FCF $955.1M - 100% SBC (~1.3% of FCF, ~$12M) = ~$943M (~$4.53/sh). SBC is exceptionally low (~0.2% of revenue), so FCF quality is high and the SBC haircut is immaterial.

conservador.note: Phase1 5% CAGR (sub-trend, freight recession lingers), Phase2 declining 5%->3%, g=2.5%. Reasonable pessimistic, not apocalyptic: ODFL keeps share but pricing/volume recovery is muted.

base.note: Phase1 8% CAGR (normalized LTL volume recovery + ~4-5% pricing, density gains), Phase2 declining 8%->4%, g=3.0%. Off a cyclically depressed FY2025 owner-FCF base.

optimista.note: Phase1 11% CAGR (strong industrial cycle rebound, May 2026 rev/day +12.3% YoY momentum persists, margin re-expansion), Phase2 11%->5%, g=3.5%.

multiple_rationale: Anchor to the ~32x 5y avg forward P/E with a modest haircut to 30x. ODFL is a best-in-class LTL compounder (ROIC ~24%, net cash, ~0.2% SBC, ~76% operating ratio) with no structural impairment — the FY2025/Q1 2026 softness is cyclical (freight recession, -5.5% organic) and demand is already re-accelerating (May rev/day +12.3% YoY). The small haircut reflects (a) a maturing share-gain runway and (b) base-rate discipline against paying full peak multiples. Applied to FY2026E EPS of ~$5.05 (consensus range $4.99-$5.11). Current 38.4x vs 32x avg = ~+20% premium, PEG ~2.4 = rich entry.
structural_change: None structural. Headwinds are cyclical: FY2025 revenue -5.5% organic, Q1 2026 -2.9%, LTL tons/day -7.7%, operating ratio worsened to 76.2% (from 75.4%). But pricing held (LTL rev/cwt +5.7%, +4.4% ex-fuel) and demand is recovering (May 2026 rev/day +12.3% YoY). Moat (density, service quality, owned terminal network), net-cash balance sheet, and ~24% ROIC remain fully intact. Capex normalizing (~$265M FY2026 guide).
sanity_notes: Implied mcap 219.52 x 0.20797B = $45.65B, matches known ~$45.4-46.0B scale (mcap_sanity_ok=true). IV/share $125.85 = ~57% of $219.52 price, well within the 30-300% magnitude band, so no shares/currency/units error. Note the large DCF-vs-multiple gap ($94.51 vs $151.50): DCF undercredits this high-ROIC compounder reinvesting for decades and runs off a cyclically depressed FY2025 owner-FCF base, while the multiple captures the franchise premium — exactly the divergence the framework flags. Weights tilted modestly to the multiple (0.55) given the proven, pristine compounder, but DCF kept meaningful (0.45) because ODFL is freight-cyclical with real capex and earnings are at a trough. CONCLUSION: at ~$220 vs reconciled IV ~$126, ODFL is materially OVERVALUED (~75% above IV); quality is elite but the price embeds a full-cycle peak multiple on trough earnings. Owner-FCF and EPS bases are aggregator-derived (FCF $955.1M, FY2025 EPS $4.86, FY2026E ~$5.05), not line-item-confirmed vs 10-K.
